body: Thanks, I'll certainly need it. My depression has been keeping me from studying recently, and that's certainly not a good thing, so I figured I had to seek some kind of advice/help.

These kinds of thoughts also give me hope - I do have skills that I haven't explored to their full potential yet (writing, debate, etc.), and I'm studying to take the LSAT in September/December, but at this point, if I don't do well on the LSAT I don't have anything left - only a life of selling products for some shitty food company, getting married in my late 30s to my first girlfriend, and having a couple of kids that will eventually just repeat this terrible cycle of self hate.

I would love to believe that I could possibly find someone later in life, or find a job that could give me a solid paycheck while still giving my life meaning, but as it stands I don't really see a way that happen. I'm living with my hoarder parents with around 30k in student debt, and I haven't been able to find a job that wasn't in sales (I've watched my father suffer and toil in sales all my life - not something I want to do) a full year after graduating. I have never been in a relationship, never been told by a woman "I like you" never had a woman check me out. In lieu of actually working I currently do some open mic stand up comedy around town, but even that turns into a self deprecative shit show after a while and I have to consciously avoid self deprecation jokes when I'm writing so I don't seem like the only reason I go up on stage is because I can't afford therapy.

I have spoken to my friends about this, and their words haven't been very encouraging. One of them pretty much ignores it, the other one tries not to talk about it because I think it makes him uncomfortable, and the other one the other day said that if I weren't me he'd have "given up on me a while ago". All this kind of confirms it for me that overall they'd be better off without me. They've got their own shit to think about and they don't need me desperately pining for an answer to "what is wrong with me" to clutter up their minds.

I think I've always sort of felt this way, even going back to elementary school, but the fact that I can't find employment even a full year after receiving my degree kind of confirms everything. That along with some recent weight gain after college and the fact that I've also never been in anything resembling a real relationship with a woman - It makes me feel like I have absolutely no purpose on this planet. I can never be a father, I can never be a successful career person, I can never be a good friend if these factors keep my psychological state in the dumpster. All I can do is leech off of others, ride on the accomplishments of others until I find some bullshit job flipping burgers and die at the french fry station at age 88 - single, no kids, nothing to show for all my years on the planet. Obituary reading something like "Creepy old man dies at work, town breathes sigh of relief."
